entity_independent_web_verification.method: Every named entity in the CURRENT passage re-verified from scratch (OSM/Nominatim, Wikidata wbsearchentities, en/sv Wikipedia insource regex search, Open Library, Exa web/people search). Nothing taken on the repair's word.
entity_independent_web_verification.Nattrand (sleeper service): CLEAR. Nominatim: empty result array. Wikidata wbsearchentities: empty. en.wikipedia insource:/Nattrand/: totalhits 0. sv.wikipedia insource: 0. Exa night-train search surfaces only real operators (Snalltaget, European Sleeper, UEX Night, RDC/Nachtexpress, VR, SJ) - no Nattrand.
entity_independent_web_verification.Vaneby Rail (operator): CLEAR as an operator/station/locality, with one disclosed near-neighbour. Nominatim q=Vaneby and q=Vaneby(umlaut) return ONLY 'Vanebyvagen' (Vanebyvagen) - a residential/unclassified road plus one bus stop in Vane-Asaka, Trollhattans kommun, Sweden. No place node, no station, no rail operator; sv.wikipedia insource 0 hits. Exa finds only a US 1850-census given name (Vaneby Harter, Allen Co., Ohio) and a forebears.io surname-variant row with 1 bearer. No collision with any rail entity.
entity_independent_web_verification.Anneke Verholt (transport economist): CLEAR. Wikidata: only 'Verholtknutten' (a Norwegian topographic feature). Exa people search returns living Dutch bearers of the surname Verholt (psychologist, production manager, PhD candidate, artist, CAD draughtsman) - none in transport, rail or economics, and no person named Anneke Verholt anywhere. Nearest transport-sector 'Anneke' hits are different surnames (van Dorp, van de Mond, Spies-Voogt).
entity_independent_web_verification.Miles Wrensham (byline): CLEAR. en.wikipedia insource:/Wrensham/: totalhits 0. Exa: 'Wrensham' occurs only as (a) a 19th-century census mis-spelling of Wrentham, Suffolk (1881 St George Union Workhouse, Towcester 1871), (b) 'Wrensham Street', Birmingham baptisms 1859, (c) a fictional locality in George Meredith's 'One of Our Conquerors' (1891), (d) a listed surname variant on a genealogy site. No living bearer, no journalist. Nearest real journalists are Miles Costello / Miles Ellingham / Myles Wren - different surnames.
entity_independent_web_verification.Slow Trains Home (title): No book or article of that exact title. Open Library q="Slow Trains Home": numFound 2, both the same 1951 novel 'The Slow Train Home' by Dorothy Cowlin (singular 'Train', definite article, unrelated genre). Disclosed as a note, not a collision.
entity_independent_web_verification.unnamed referents: 'the capital', 'the northern coast', 'weekly current-affairs magazine' carry no real-world referent - confirmed by reading, nothing to verify.

findings.claim: The repair asserts the fresh entityfix-tagged regate lines are the last records for this unit in verdicts-vfinal/. That is true for verdicts-gstem, verdicts-gdistractor, verdicts-gkey-1 and verdicts-gkey-2, but verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl was never regenerated.
findings.evidence: git status shows verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl unmodified while the other four are M. Its last elf-b3-002 records (lines 34-38) are executed_by 'claude-opus-4-8/G-KEY-regate0724', vote 2 - the pre-rename generation. Both vote legs did re-run under entityfix and agreed (C/A/D/B/C), so the resolved fold would be unchanged in substance.
findings.why: A consumer that treats verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl as the authoritative merged G-KEY ledger attributes this unit's key verdicts to the pre-rename passage. No substantive risk here because options and keys are byte-identical, but the recency assertion is not universally true across verdicts-vfinal/.

findings.claim: The entityfix lines appended to verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl use target 'q1'..'q5' (no colon), deviating from the 'q:1' convention used by every other record in verdicts-vfinal/ - including their own sibling lines in verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl.
findings.evidence: verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl lines 20-24: "target": "q1" ... "q5"; verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl lines 20-24: "target": "q:1" ... "q:5"; all 19 preceding lines in gkey-1 use 'q:n'.
findings.why: Any fold that joins the two vote legs on (candidate_id, gate, target) will fail to pair the vote-1 and vote-2 entityfix records for this unit and could silently drop or double-count a leg.

findings.claim: The note's flat statement "'Vaneby' - no Swedish/Norwegian locality, station or rail operator" is correct as written, but the stem is a real Swedish toponym element that appears in a transport-name context.
findings.evidence: Nominatim q=Vaneby returns five 'Vanebyvagen' (Vanebyvagen) features - residential/unclassified/service road plus a bus_stop - in Vane-Asaka, Trollhattans kommun, Vastra Gotalands lan, Sweden. No place node named Vaneby, no station, no operator; sv.wikipedia has no article.
findings.why: Not a collision of the Aurora/Halden class (no company, no station, no service), so the repair's decision stands - but a future bank-wide sweep that fuzz-matches toponym stems will surface it, and the note reads more absolutely than the evidence supports.

findings.claim: The note's claim that the title 'Slow Trains Home' matches no real book is literally true, but there is a near-miss it does not mention.
findings.evidence: Open Library q="Slow Trains Home" returns numFound 2, both the same work: 'The Slow Train Home', Dorothy Cowlin, first published 1951 (singular 'Train', definite article).
findings.why: Different title string, different domain (a mid-century English novel, not night-train journalism), 75 years old - no student-facing confusion risk. Recorded so the near-miss is on file rather than rediscovered as a surprise.
